summary: This bill requires the President to identify within 180 days any senior Pakistani government, military, or security officials responsible for gross human rights violations that undermine democracy and then authorizes sanctions against them under the Global Magnitsky Act.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes no new US government programs, appropriations, or expenditures. Any administrative costs for sanctions reporting would be negligible and incidental. It has no bearing on government spending levels.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures of any kind.
No provisions relate to US healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill does not address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
A narrow exception preserves admission of aliens only to meet UN headquarters obligations; this is a technical carve-out, not a change to US immigration policy or pathways.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not authorize, increase, or decrease US military or defense spending.
No environmental or climate provisions are present.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policy.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy provisions exist.
The bill contains no drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance measures.
While the bill references due-process concerns in Pakistan, it does not alter US criminal sentencing, policing, or justice-system policy.
Targeted sanctions on individuals may have incidental effects on specific transactions but do not establish new US trade, tariff, or globalization policy.
No deficit, debt-ceiling, or fiscal-policy provisions are included.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals in the United States.
The legislation imposes sanctions on specific Pakistani officials but does not authorize, expand, reduce, or condition US foreign assistance to Pakistan or any other country.
The bill expresses support for democratic elections in Pakistan and condemns interference there; it does not alter US voting access, voter ID, or election procedures.
References to internet restrictions in Pakistan are factual findings only and do not change US technology regulation or data-privacy policy.
No labor, union, or workplace provisions are present.
The bill notes religious-minority issues in Pakistan as background but does not modify US religious-liberty or anti-discrimination law.
